messages:
alyssa: heads-up — noticed a perf regression in the canary after yesterday's model push (v4.2.1). p50 for long sequences (>1500 tokens) jumped ~3x in us-west-2. filing here so runtime+infra can triage.

mikael: ack. is this only seq>1500? any change in request distribution or batching rates?

alyssa: yep mostly long tails. overall qps steady. batching rate increased a bit because of a spike in small chat completions earlier, but the weird part is CPU/GPU kernels show a hot path on the attention matmul for the older kernel variant.

tara: @mikael can you pull profiler traces from the canary nodes? i want to see kernel selection decisions and kv-cache hit/miss stats.

infra-bot: Canary rollout (v4.2.1) deployed to 10% in us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T22:03:20Z. Health: green -> degraded (22:03:40Z). Alerts: latency.p50 > baseline (3x) for seqlen>1500.

mikael: attaching trimmed perf snippet from the node where we repro'd it (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17 22:05:02] kernel_select: selected=matmul_fused_v1 fallback=matmul_fast_v2
[2026-03-17 22:05:02] seq_len=1600 avg_batch=4 kv_cache_hits=0.62 kv_cache_prefetch=0.03
[2026-03-17 22:05:02] kernel_time_ms: matmul_fused_v1=18.9 matmul_fast_v2=6.2
```
This is the surprising bit — the runtime picked fused_v1 which is slower for this seq/batch shape. need to see why selector favored it.

kevin: did the tokenizer change in v4.2 -> v4.2.1? token boundaries can shift and change effective seq distribution.

alyssa: yes — v4.2.1 moved to a new padding/trailing-space normalization to fix hallucination on code blocks. that increased avg tokenization by ~5% and changed some long-turn samples to be longer.

jordan: i pulled kernel selector logs — looks like the selector uses a cached heuristic key: (model_id, architecture, batch_hint, seq_bucket). the tokenizer change pushed many requests into a different seq_bucket (1500-2000) that we hadn't optimized for with fallback thresholds.

tara: aha. so two effects: (1) different seq bucket distribution; (2) runtime cached a kernel choice from older perf profile that assumed higher kv_cache_hit rate. KV cache behavior matters: lower hits means more matmul sizes and different memory access patterns.

mikael: can we repro locally by forcing seqlen 1600, batch=1..6 and running selector bench? i'll run across GPUs with both kernels.

alyssa: started a quick canary rollback to v4.2 (partial) to reduce user impact. canary-bot: rollback initiated at 22:06:14Z, target 50% of canary hosts.

infra-bot: rolling metrics: p50 returning to baseline on rollback targets. overall canary still mixed until all hosts converge.

kevin: for root cause doc: tokenizer changed distribution -> requests hit a seq_bucket we hadn't profiled -> selector cached suboptimal kernel (fused_v1) for that key -> combined with reduced kv_cache_hits for long sequences caused 3x p50. proposed fixes: update selector heuristics, add per-bucket fallback thresholds, expand perf matrix in model onboarding.

jordan: agree. also add a quick guard: if real-time profiler detects chosen kernel slower than alternate by >1.5x for X samples, auto-switch and emit metric.

tara: i'll open a runtime PR to add runtime self-check and to invalidate selector cache on model metadata changes (tokenizer/normalization flags). mikael please add microbench data to the PR: results for batch 1..8, seq 128..2048, kv-hit 0.2/0.5/0.9 for both kernels.

mikael: on it. will paste bench results in the PR. early local numbers show fused_v1 slower for seq>1024 except at very high batch sizes.

alyssa: thanks all. next steps: (1) keep canary rollback until we've validated selector fix; (2) runtime PR + perf bench; (3) model onboarding checklist update to include tokenizer-impact checks. tagging @kevin to coordinate update to onboarding docs.

kevin: will update onboarding doc and add a short eval harness that computes seq-bucket shifts vs baseline. also will add a note to changelog: "tokenizer normalizations can affect seq buckets — run perf gating." :memo:

alyssa: closing the loop once PR is in and canary metrics stabilize. thanks. :raised_hands:
